info.name: Expense Claims API
info.description: Auth and claim endpoints. Import the matching environment, set its `password` (the seed password), run '1. Auth' first, then '2. Claims' in order. Every error has { error: { code, message, requestId, details? } }.

exec: // Today's date (UTC) for line item dates: they must not be in the future

request.description: Liveness check used by Docker and load balancers. Needs no token and is not logged.
Saves the JWT in {{token}}. Run this first. Needs the `password` environment variable.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("claimantEmail")); });

request.description: Saves a second claimant's token in {{tokenOther}}, used by the isolation checks.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("claimant2Email")); });

request.description: Saves an approver's token in {{tokenApprover}}, used by the role checks.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("approverEmail")); });

request.description: Saves the level-2 approver's token in {{tokenApprover2}}. Meera only gets a step after Ravi (level 1) approved.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the level-2 approver", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("approver2Email")); pm.expect(body.user.approvalLevel).to.eql(2); });

pm.test("Returns the logged-in user without a password hash", function () { const u = pm.response.json().user; pm.expect(u.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("claimantEmail")); pm.expect(u).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });

request.description: Saves {{claimId}} and {{itemId}} (the first line item) for the next requests. The total is computed by the server; sending `total` is rejected.

exec: pm.test("Draft with a computed total of 30.50", function () { pm.expect(claim.status).to.eql("DRAFT"); pm.expect(claim.total).to.eql("30.50"); pm.expect(claim.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); });

item.name: Create claim with no items (empty draft)

request.description: Saves {{emptyClaimId}}: the 'Delete' request below removes THIS draft, so the main test claim survives for the line item requests.

exec: pm.test("Total is 0.00 with no items", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("0.00"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(0); });

pm.test("Has data and pagination, no line items in the list", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data).to.be.an("array"); pm.expect(b.pagination).to.have.all.keys("page","pageSize","totalItems","totalPages"); if (b.data.length) { pm.expect(b.data[0]).to.have.property("lineItemCount"); pm.expect(b.data[0]).to.not.have.property("lineItems"); } });
pm.test("Same claim with its items", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("claimId")); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("30.50"); });

request.description: Only the title can be edited (the total is derived, the status follows the workflow). Works on any claim except an APPROVED one; a title change leaves the total unchanged, so an approval chain is not reset.

exec: pm.test("Title changed, total and items untouched", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.title).to.eql("Postman test claim (renamed)"); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("30.50"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c.status).to.eql("DRAFT"); });

item.name: Delete a claim (DELETE, the empty draft)

request.description: Only a DRAFT can be deleted. A submitted claim (pending, rejected or approved) is part of the audit trail and returns 409.
The body is ONE line item. The date uses {{today}}, which a collection pre-request script sets.

exec: pm.test("Total went up by 7.25 (30.50 -> 37.75), 3 items", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("37.75"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(3); });

item.name: Update a line item: only the amount (PATCH)

request.description: PATCH changes only the fields you send (at least one of date, category, amount, description). This example sends just the amount; the next request changes several fields.

exec: pm.test("Total is now 45.25 (the 12.50 item became 20.00)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().total).to.eql("45.25"); });

item.name: Update a line item: several fields at once (PATCH)

request.description: Any combination of date, category, amount and description. Fields you leave out stay as they are.

exec: pm.test("Total unchanged (45.25): the amount was not touched", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().total).to.eql("45.25"); });

pm.test("Description, category and date changed together", function () { const item = pm.response.json().lineItems.find(i => i.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("itemId")); pm.expect(item.description).to.eql("Team lunch"); pm.expect(item.category).to.eql("TRAVEL"); pm.expect(item.date).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("today")); pm.expect(item.amount).to.eql("20.00"); });

pm.test("Item is gone and total recomputed (45.25 - 20.00 = 25.25)", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("25.25"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c.lineItems.map(i => i.id)).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("itemId")); });

request.description: Uses {{claimId}} from the claims folders (it still has line items). The server builds the approval chain from the total: level 1 approver PENDING, higher levels WAITING.

exec: pm.test("Now pending approval, submittedAt set, total is a string", function () { pm.expect(claim.status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); pm.expect(claim.submittedAt).to.not.eql(null); pm.expect(claim.total).to.be.a("string"); });

request.description: Only a DRAFT can be submitted; a double click or retry is refused.

item.name: Rename the submitted claim -> 200 (title only, total unchanged)

request.description: A claim awaiting approval can be edited. A title change does not change the total, so the approval chain is NOT reset.

exec: pm.test("Still pending, title changed, total unchanged", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); pm.expect(c.title).to.eql("Postman test claim (renamed while pending)"); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("submitTotal")); });

item.name: Change an item's amount on the submitted claim -> 200 (chain reset)

request.description: The total changes, so every approval so far is void and the chain restarts from level 1 (same approvers, new chainVersion; two history rows: CLAIM_UPDATED and APPROVAL_CHAIN_RESET). No endpoint shows approvals yet, so this request checks the new total.

exec: pm.test("Still pending, new amount and a different total", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); const item = c.lineItems.find(function (i) { return i.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("submitItemId"); }); pm.expect(item.amount).to.eql("777.77"); pm.expect(c.total).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("submitTotal")); });

request.description: A submitted claim is part of the audit trail and is never deleted.

item.name: Create an empty draft for the submit check

request.description: Saves {{emptyDraftId}}: a draft with no line items.

item.name: Submit a claim with no line items -> 422 NO_LINE_ITEMS
Create a one-item claim (for the last-item rule)

request.description: Saves {{oneItemClaimId}} and {{oneItemId}}.
A claim awaiting approval must keep at least one line item. Nothing changes (the chain is not reset).

item.name: Add a second item to the pending claim -> 201

exec: pm.test("Two items, total 65.00", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("65.00"); });

request.description: Allowed, because another item remains.

exec: pm.test("One item left, total 25.00", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("25.00"); });

request.description: Uses the approver token from the login request. Lists only approvals that wait for THIS approver now (a level-2 step appears only after level 1 approved). Needs {{claimId}} submitted in folder 4; saves {{approvalId}} (my step of that claim).

exec: pm.test("Has data and pagination", function () { pm.expect(body.data).to.be.an("array"); pm.expect(body.pagination).to.have.all.keys("page","pageSize","totalItems","totalPages"); });

pm.test("Every entry is a PENDING step of mine with a claim summary", function () { body.data.forEach(function (a) { pm.expect(a.status).to.eql("PENDING"); pm.expect(a.claim).to.have.all.keys("id","claimNumber","title","total","submittedAt","claimantName"); pm.expect(a.claim.total).to.be.a("string"); }); });

pm.test("The claim submitted earlier is waiting for me", function () { const ids = body.data.map(function (a) { return a.claim.id; }); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("claimId")); });
const mine = body.data.find(function (a) { return a.claim.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("claimId"); }); if (mine) { pm.collectionVariables.set("approvalId", mine.id); }

item.name: Approve my step of the claim

request.description: One level claims (total under 10,000) are approved and locked right away. Claims over 10,000 move to the next level.

exec: pm.test("Step approved; claim moves on or is approved", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql("APPROVED"); pm.expect(b.decidedAt).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(["PENDING_APPROVAL","APPROVED"]).to.include(b.claim.status); });

item.name: Approve the same step again -> 409 APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING

request.description: A decided step cannot be decided twice (double click and retry safe).
Saves {{rejectClaimId}}. This mini flow has its own claim, so it does not depend on the approve requests above.

item.name: Find my step of it (approver queue)

request.description: Saves {{rejectApprovalId}}.

exec: pm.test("The submitted claim is waiting for me", function () { pm.expect(mine).to.not.eql(undefined); });

request.description: A reason is required, so the claimant knows what to fix. Nothing changes.
Earlier approvals stay as they were; the steps still open become INVALIDATED.

exec: pm.test("Step rejected with the reason, claim rejected", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql("REJECTED"); pm.expect(b.reason).to.eql("Receipt is missing"); pm.expect(b.claim.status).to.eql("REJECTED"); });

item.name: Claimant fixes the rejected claim -> 200 (still REJECTED)

request.description: Uses the claimant token (the default).

exec: pm.test("Edited and still rejected (it has no live chain until resubmit)", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql("REJECTED"); pm.expect(b.title).to.eql("Postman claim (fixed after rejection)"); });

item.name: Rejected claim shows why it was rejected

request.description: GET /claims/:id returns lastRejection whenever the claim has ever been rejected.

exec: pm.test("lastRejection has the reason, level and who rejected it", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql("REJECTED"); pm.expect(lr.reason).to.eql("Receipt is missing"); pm.expect(lr.level).to.eql(1); pm.expect(lr.rejectedBy).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(lr.rejectedAt).to.be.a("string"); });

request.description: Starts a new approval chain from level 1 with the same approvers. The first submittedAt and the earlier approvals are kept.
Only a rejected claim can be resubmitted.

item.name: The rejection is still shown after the resubmit

exec: pm.test("Pending again, but the last rejection is kept", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); pm.expect(lr.reason).to.eql("Receipt is missing"); });

item.name: The approver sees the resubmitted claim again

exec: pm.test("Back in the approver queue", function () { const ids = pm.response.json().data.map(function (a) { return a.claim.id; }); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("rejectClaimId")); });

request.description: From 10,000 up a claim needs two levels. Note: this flow ends with an APPROVED claim, which the database locks for good, so every run leaves one approved claim behind.

item.name: Two levels: level-2 approver does not see it yet

exec: pm.test("Not in the level-2 queue while level 1 is open", function () { const ids = pm.response.json().data.map(function (a) { return a.claim.id; }); pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); });

item.name: Two levels: level-1 approver finds the step

request.description: Saves {{twoL1ApprovalId}}.

exec: pm.test("A level-1 step is waiting for Ravi", function () { pm.expect(mine).to.not.eql(undefined); pm.expect(mine.level).to.eql(1); });

pm.test("Level 1 approved, the claim is still pending", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.level).to.eql(1); pm.expect(b.claim.status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); pm.expect(b.claim.approvedAt).to.eql(null); });

item.name: Two levels: level-2 approver now finds the step

request.description: Saves {{twoL2ApprovalId}}.

exec: pm.test("A level-2 step is waiting for Meera", function () { pm.expect(mine).to.not.eql(undefined); pm.expect(mine.level).to.eql(2); });

item.name: Two levels: level 2 approves -> claim APPROVED

exec: pm.test("Last level approved: the claim is approved", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.level).to.eql(2); pm.expect(b.claim.status).to.eql("APPROVED"); pm.expect(b.claim.approvedAt).to.be.a("string"); });

item.name: Two levels: claimant edits the approved claim -> 409 CLAIM_LOCKED

request.description: An approved claim is locked (service rule, with a database trigger behind it). Uses the claimant token (the default).

item.name: 6. Visibility and filters (run after the approvals folder)

request.description: Saves Sana's token in {{tokenApprover3}}. Sana is Bilal's level-1 approver, so she has no step on Asha's claims.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the approver", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("approver3Email")); pm.expect(body.user.role).to.eql("APPROVER"); });

request.description: Saves Farah's token in {{tokenFinance}}. Finance can read every claim.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the finance", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("financeEmail")); pm.expect(body.user.role).to.eql("FINANCE"); });

item.name: Level-1 approver reads a claim on their chain -> 200

request.description: Run after the approvals folder. Ravi approved level 1 of this claim.

exec: pm.test("The claim with its items", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); pm.expect(c.lineItems).to.be.an("array"); });

item.name: Level-2 approver reads the same claim -> 200
Approver with no step on it reads it -> 404

request.description: Approver-by-ID isolation: Sana is not on this claim's chain.

exec: pm.test("NOT_FOUND, same answer as a missing claim", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql("NOT_FOUND"); });

item.name: Approver lists claims: only ones they are on

exec: pm.test("Lists the claim they approved", function () { const ids = pm.response.json().data.map(c => c.id); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); });

item.name: Other approver lists claims: not this one

exec: pm.test("Does not list a claim they have no step on", function () { const ids = pm.response.json().data.map(c => c.id); pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); });
pm.test("Finance sees the claim", function () { const ids = pm.response.json().data.map(c => c.id); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); });

pm.test("Every claim is APPROVED and the approved one is there", function () { const data = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(data.every(c => c.status === "APPROVED")).to.eql(true); pm.expect(data.map(c => c.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); });

item.name: Filter by status=DRAFT leaves it out

exec: pm.test("Only drafts, not the approved claim", function () { const data = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(data.every(c => c.status === "DRAFT")).to.eql(true); pm.expect(data.map(c => c.id)).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); });

request.description: from and to are inclusive UTC days of submittedAt.

exec: pm.test("Submitted claims only (a draft has no submittedAt) and the approved one is there", function () { const data = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(data.every(c => c.submittedAt !== null)).to.eql(true); pm.expect(data.map(c => c.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("twoLevelClaimId")); });

item.name: Filter from a date in the future -> empty page

exec: pm.test("No claims", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data).to.have.length(0); pm.expect(b.pagination.totalItems).to.eql(0); });

item.name: 7. Receipts (run after the visibility folder; select a file where noted)
Create a claim with one item for the receipts

exec: pm.test("A new item has no receipts yet", function () { pm.expect(c.lineItems[0].receipts).to.eql([]); });

request.description: Select any PNG, JPEG or PDF (up to 5 MB) in the file field of the Body tab before sending.

exec: pm.test("Metadata only: no stored name or path", function () { pm.expect(r).to.have.keys(["id", "lineItemId", "originalName", "mimeType", "sizeBytes", "uploadedAt"]); pm.expect(r.lineItemId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("receiptItemId")); });

pm.test("The item shows the receipt", function () { const receipts = pm.response.json().lineItems[0].receipts; pm.expect(receipts).to.have.length(1); pm.expect(receipts[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("receiptId")); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(receipts)).to.not.include("storedName"); });

pm.test("Sent as a private attachment", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Content-Disposition")).to.include("attachment"); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Cache-Control")).to.include("private"); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Content-Type")).to.match(/^(image\/png|image\/jpeg|application\/pdf)/); });

request.description: Needs 'Login as finance' (folder 6).

item.name: Approver with no step on it downloads it -> 404

request.description: Needs 'Login as second approver (Sana)' (folder 6). Sana has no step on Asha's claims.

exec: pm.test("NOT_FOUND, same as a missing receipt", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql("NOT_FOUND"); });

item.name: Another claimant uploads to my item -> 404 (select a file)

request.description: Select any PNG, JPEG or PDF (up to 5 MB) in the file field of the Body tab before sending. Without a file this returns 400 instead.

item.name: 8. Finance export (run after the approvals folder)

request.description: Saves Farah's token in {{tokenFinance}}. Finance can read every claim.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the finance", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("financeEmail")); pm.expect(body.user.role).to.eql("FINANCE"); });

request.description: Needs 'Login as finance (Farah)', the first request in this folder. The period is the final approval date: from and to are both included, in UTC.

exec: pm.test("Starts with the header row", function () { pm.expect(text.split("\r\n")[0]).to.eql("claimNumber,claimId,title,claimantName,claimantEmail,submittedAt,approvedAt,total,lineItemCount"); });

pm.test("Only approved claims: the rejected claim from the approvals folder is not in it", function () { const id = pm.collectionVariables.get("rejectClaimId"); if (id) { pm.expect(text).to.not.include(id); } });

item.name: Finance exports a period with nothing approved -> header only

exec: pm.test("Reports each bad field with its path", function () { const paths = pm.response.json().error.details.map(d => d.path); ["lineItems.0.date","lineItems.0.category","lineItems.0.amount","lineItems.0.description"].forEach(p => pm.expect(paths).to.include(p)); });

request.description: A trailing comma is not valid JSON.

item.name: Claim id that is not a UUID -> 400

request.description: Needs 'Login as second claimant'. Refused in the query itself: 404, not 403.
Needs 'Login as approver'.

item.name: Update the claim with an empty body -> 400

request.description: The status follows the workflow; a client can never set it.
Out-of-scope claims look like they do not exist (404, not 403).

item.name: Submit with an id that is not a UUID -> 400

request.description: The queue is for approvers only (default token is the claimant's).
Only approvers can approve (default token is the claimant's).
An approval that does not exist, or belongs to another approver, looks the same: 404.

item.name: Approve with an id that is not a UUID -> 400

request.description: Only approvers can reject (default token is the claimant's).
Schemas are strict: unknown fields are refused.

item.name: Level-2 approver approves a level-1 step -> 404

request.description: Someone else's step looks the same as a missing one.
Uses the empty draft from the submit folder. Only a rejected claim can be resubmitted.

item.name: List with from later than to -> 400
List with an unknown query field -> 400

request.description: Needs 'Login as finance'. Finance is read-only.

item.name: Update a field that cannot be edited (claimId) -> 400

request.description: Needs a claim from the receipts folder (receiptItemId).

item.name: Upload to an id that is not a UUID -> 400
Download with an id that is not a UUID -> 400
Export with an unknown query field -> 400
